Theme

Latin word

forēnsis

forēnsis, forēnse

adjective, third declension

formal (of dress): worn in public, against what one wears at home; of the courts and public business

In this lexicon

  • formal

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 33.47.10: vestītū forēnsī; Cic. Fin. 2.77: ut vestītum … aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem

  • legal

    also used · classical · Cic. Or. 170: ōrātiō jūdiciālis et forēnsis (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • ut vestītum, sīc sententiam habeās aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem

    that you should have one opinion for home and another for public, as you do with your clothesCic. Fin. 2.77

    In the entry for formal

  • reliqua sunt epistulārum genera duo, quae mē magnō opere dēlectant, ūnum familiāre et jocōsum, alterum sevērum et grave

    there remain two kinds of letter which give me great pleasure, one familiar and joking, the other serious and formalCic. Fam. 2.4.1

    In the entry for formal

  • prīmīs tenebrīs vestītū forēnsī ad portam cum duōbus comitibus ignārīs cōnsiliī est ēgressus

    as soon as it was dark he went out to the gate, in his ordinary public dress, with two companions who knew nothing of his planLiv. 33.47.10
